title: Threshold-driven fallback automation and adaptive circuit orchestration
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Client-facing routes occasionally experience bursts of 429s, request timeouts, or elevated error rates during region-level congestion and degraded model variants. Without automated fallback and well-scoped circuit breakers, customers see degraded latency and tail errors.

Goal: Implement an automated, threshold-driven fallback and circuit orchestration system that: (1) detects and classifies 429s / timeouts / error spikes per region, per model variant, and per customer tier; (2) triggers safe fallbacks to pre-configured model variants or alternate regions; (3) applies circuit hysteresis and gradual unwind to avoid oscillation; (4) exposes observability and alerting for SRE/PM to tune thresholds.

Success metrics (for rollout): reduce P50/P95 latency regressions during region incidents by >= 30%, reduce customer-visible 5xx+429 error bursts by >= 60% during incidents, and no more than 1% false-positive fallback activations in production traffic over a 7-day window.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: per-route, per-region, per-model-variant rolling metrics (requests, 429s, 5xx, timeouts, avg latency) emitted at 10s granularity to metrics pipeline.

Detection rules: configurable sliding-window rules supporting multiple aggregations (rate, pct, moving-average) and multi-window confirmation (e.g., 2x 1-minute windows) for 429s, latency, and error-rate triggers.

Actions: on trigger, system must be able to: apply model-variant fallback, route to alternate region, or open a circuit for the route+tier combination within <2s of decision; decisions must be logged and auditable.
Hysteresis: circuit-open duration and unwind policy must be configurable and support exponential backoff plus a slow-probe traffic path to validate recovery.
Safety: support manual override and immediate rollback via Console; require canary gating for rollout to >= 5% of traffic before global enablement.
Testing: end-to-end fault-injection test demonstrating a 429 spike triggers fallback and subsequent unwind when healthy in staging environment.
Monitoring: dashboard with timeline of triggers, circuit states, counts of fallbacks, and per-customer impact; automated alerts for mass fallback activations (>3 regions or >5% global traffic).
Docs: design doc and runbook published; runbook includes SRE debugging steps and rollback instructions.
implementation_notes: Detection logic: implement multi-tier rules engine in routing-plane service using decaying counters + reservoir sampling for latency percentiles to avoid being skewed by bursts.
429 handling: treat sustained 429 rate above configured per-route threshold as a rate-limit event vs model error; prefer regional reroute or lower-capacity variant before opening circuit globally.
Timeouts: correlate timeouts with downstream GPU queue depth and kernel execution latency; include token-size weighted metrics to avoid punishing large-context requests.

Circuit state: maintain local fast-path cache for circuit state in the router with periodic sync to central control-plane; use vector clock stamping to avoid split-brain during control-plane partition.
Unwind policy: use phased unwind: slow-probe (0.1% traffic), ramp (1%, 5%), full (100%) with health-check gating. Implement jittered timers to avoid synchronized retries across nodes.
Config: expose policy as JSON schema in Console: thresholds, windows, actions (fallback_variant, region, open_circuit), cooldowns, and canary_percent.
Telemetry: add structured logs for each decision: reason, metric snapshot, affected routes, pre/post model variant, and decision latency; link to existing tracing spans for request path.
Integration: relies on metrics ingestion (ENG-19877) and route-protection primitives (ENG-21534); add e2e tests in runtime repo and a chaos experiment in staging.
comments: 2026-03-01 Ava Chen: Initial spike analysis attached. Observed two region-level 429 bursts in Feb producing ~4x healthy error-rate for 7 minutes. Concluded need for multi-window confirmation to avoid false positives.

2026-03-03 Diego Rivera: Pushed prototype of sliding-window counters and moving-average latency estimator in branch runtime/feat/fallback-rules. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8912
2026-03-05 Sanjana Patel (PM): Reviewed prototype; requested per-customer tier exemptions and explicit opt-out flag for enterprise customers with dedicated capacity.

2026-03-07 Design review notes: avoid route-wide aggressive circuit opens; prefer per-model-variant then per-region, then tier escalation. Add UI for viewing active circuits and decision rationales. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Threshold+Fallback+Design

2026-03-10 QA: Wrote fault-injection test that simulates 429 flood for 90s; fallback to lower-capacity variant occurred but unwind oscillated. Need to implement exponential cooldown and jittering to fix oscillation.

2026-03-12 Diego Rivera: Implemented exponential backoff and slow-probe flow. Instrumentation added (10s granularity metrics). Deployed to staging for canary at 2% traffic. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ops/fallbacks?orgId=1

2026-03-13 SRE comment (Mikhail Ivanov): Alert thresholds proposed: trigger P1 when >=3 routes open across >=2 regions or when global fallback rate >5% for 15m. Also suggested adding synthetic probes to detect silent degradation.
